relevance_note: Supplementary Table 1 gives individual-level data (sex, age, severity, stomatitis, abdominal symptoms, medication) for 16 labelled patients ('Characteristics and microbiome diversity of the patients with HA20 and their relatives'), so in-scope people are described individually even though no TNFAIP3 variant is printed.
method_note: A Python script in my scratch directory transcribed Supplementary Table 1 (31 rows: 16 patients P3-P22 and 15 relatives labelled P3-fa ... P22-sib); I checked its cell values against the table by eye and against the text (counts of severity 4/4/5, stomatitis 11/13, abdominal symptoms 8/13, probiotics 1, immunosuppressants 5, median ages 19 and 36 all reproduce for the 13 analysed patients and 13 relatives). Scope: all 16 patients have an HA20 diagnosis; the 15 relatives are described in relation to them ('healthy family members'), so they get rows. Two further patients and two family members who agreed to participate but gave no sample, and the 22 patients of Kadowaki et al. (2018), are not individually described and get no rows. Variants: the paper prints no TNFAIP3 variant, does not use the words variant or mutation, and does not tie a specific TNFAIP3 variant to any person (only that HA20 is a disease of A20, encoded by TNFAIP3), so the variants table is empty; the variants are presumably in the earlier report, which I did not use. Ages: the 'Age' column is 'age at the sample collection' (Methods), recorded as age at last evaluation; years per the text's medians and the Discussion ('4, 1, and 3 years old'). Severity (mild/moderate/severe) is the authors' composite classification defined with 'e.g.' and 'and/or' examples; it was not recorded as a phenotypic feature and no checklist item was inferred from it. 'Stomatitis' was recorded as its own feature and not mapped to the checklist item 'oral ulcers' (not the same term); 'Abdominal symptoms' was not mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' (the authors state abdominal symptoms 'do not necessarily reflect the exact intestinal condition'). Hence every checklist row is 'not reported'. The '\-' cells for relatives (Severity, Stomatitis, Abdominal symptoms) are not defined in the legend, so they were treated as not reported; NA cells as not reported. Relatives are called 'healthy' but no feature was excluded from that word. 'Nobody but an excluded younger brother (P22-sib) has food allergies' was used only as an observed feature for P22-sib; I did not infer exclusion for the other participants because the group is not named explicitly. Group counts (autoantibodies in 4 vs 5 unnamed patients; H. parainfluenzae carriage) were not attributed to individuals. is_proband is false for relatives (rule 5) and null for patients (no proband named). Country 'Japan' comes from the statement that the nine families are in Japan, applied to all participants from those families. Treatment summaries copy the antibiotic, probiotic and immunosuppressant cells verbatim (abbreviations as printed; legend: CFPN-PI Cefcapene Pivoxil, MTX methotrexate, PSL prednisolone, CyA cyclosporin A, etc.). P8 and P9 share a mother (P8/P9-mo) but no family label is printed, so family_label is not reported. A sibling 'whose genetic information is unknown' cannot be identified among the table rows. cohort_size_as_stated = 18 patients who agreed to participate (36 individuals in total); n_patients_reported = 16 with samples. Contradiction noted (study level only): Tables 1 and 2 give 'Severity (severe or not) | 5 (28%)' and 'Immunosuppressants | 5 (28%)', but 5 of 13 is 38%.
